title: radio.py: GE cache is per (rx, tx), later GE rules skipped
description:
## Problem

9098.28 cached Gilbert-Elliott survival per `(rx_node_id, tx_id)` so a 1 ms poll does not re-enter `apply`. `_apply_live_chaos` uses that one bool for every `isinstance(rule, GilbertElliottRule)`:

```python
if isinstance(rule, GilbertElliottRule):
    if key in ge_cache:
        if not ge_cache[key]:
            dropped.add(key)
            return None
        continue   # skips THIS and any later GE on the same (rx, tx)
    applied = self._apply_ge_independent(...)
    ge_cache[key] = applied is not None
```

`ChaosEngine` is documented to compose rules in insertion order; any rule returning None drops. Two GE rules (global urban fade + per-node burst, or two `node_id` filters) are legal.

If the first GE survives, `ge_cache[key] is True`. The next GE hits the cache and `continue`s: it never `apply()`s. A second GE that would have dropped is ignored. If the first GE drops, tombstone returns None (second GE does not run — correct fail-closed). The hole is survival of GE1 masking GE2.

9098.39 walks every neighbor with an independent shim; it does not namespace the radio cache by `rule.id`. `test_radio.py` GE tests add a single `GilbertElliottRule`.

## Why this is security (fault-injection oracle)

Stacked GE is how a scenario injects a mesh-wide fade plus a targeted node burst. Radio.py makes the second rule a no-op whenever the first packet lived. Delivery_rate / compare_metrics then measure only the first GE, so a "harder" chaos config can be bit-identical to the easier one. That is false confidence in OSCORE/partition tests that add a second burst rule.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_apply_live_chaos` GE cache keyed only on `(rx, tx)`)
- `python/tests/sim/test_radio.py` (one GE rule per test)
design: Key _ge_survived by (rx_node_id, tx_id, rule.id) or keep a small per-rule dict. On a cache hit, skip only that GilbertElliottRule, then continue the loop so a later GE/Drop/Jam still runs. A False from any GE still tombstones _dropped_rx for the (rx, tx) pair (fail-closed). Do not share one bool across all GE rules. Do not re-open 9098.28 (poll re-roll) or 9098.39 (one chain for every neighbor).
acceptance_criteria: Two GilbertElliottRule instances on one ChaosEngine both run for a given (rx, tx). If the first survives and the second is configured to always drop (loss_prob_good=1, p_good_to_bad=0), get_rx_result is None. If both would survive, delivery still happens and 9098.28 still holds: each rule's apply is once per (rx, tx), not per poll. Cache keys include rule identity (rule.id) or decisions are stored per rule. test_radio.py covers two GE rules, not only one.
